title: A stronger field on a wire
hook: Change magnetic-field magnitude and predict force magnitude on the wire.
misconception: force magnitude on the wire stays fixed when magnetic-field magnitude doubles.
objective: Apply F = BIL to compare force magnitude on the wire when magnetic-field magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a straight wire of fixed length carrying fixed current perpendicular to the field, F = BIL. When magnetic-field magnitude doubles, force magnitude on the wire becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F = BIL; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a straight wire of fixed length carrying fixed current perpendicular to the field, with a nonzero initial result. If magnetic-field magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on force magnitude on the wire?
recall.why: Apply F = BIL under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
